lines.style: Speak English as a cheerful Japanese learner greeting a friend on New Year's morning, bright and warm. Say every word exactly as written: 'Ear' is the body part and starts directly on the vowel, like Japanese 'iyaa', with NO 'y' sound before it, so a listener clearly hears 'Happy New Ear!' Slightly flat, syllable-by-syllable Japanese-style timing. Natural, not a caricature.

Speak fluent General American English like a native speaker saying one word clearly and calmly, as in a pronunciation lesson. 'Year' starts with a clear, quick 'y' glide as in 'yes' (tongue high near the roof of the mouth), then the vowel and an American r. Natural, not exaggerated.

Speak English as a Japanese learner saying one word on its own, as in a pronunciation lesson. Say 'Ear' (the body part) like Japanese 'iyaa': start directly on the vowel 'ee' with NO 'y' sound before it, then an open 'ah', no American r. Natural, not a caricature.
